you need 4 pieces of armour which are acquired from the chests(purchased with roman coins 2k - 2.5k roman coins each chest) at the coliseum:

comments.author: Snipe
comments.body: For those people that don't know how to get certain titles: Meister titles and adept require certain production skills to be max rank (r15) (adept is alchemy). Circumliner is given to any player who completes the Circumliner event, which is started by talking to your nation king after getting SEA permit. Company membership title is given when one's company is above r4 (regardless of one's levels). Marechal is given after 50 wins (or battles, not sure) in battle campaign. Cassador is given when one kills 50 pirates by sea battle (can be same pirate or different). Graduate titles are given to players who completed schools of the required topic. Student is given to one who is still in school and the only title that is automatically removed (after one completes all three courses in school. Shipwreck hunter: complete 100 sw. Quip.... Either gotten by unlocking a inland city or from a quest chain (not sure). Oceloti is given to a player completing a long quest chain (end of chain also gives the jaguar costume thingy). Flower C: in the 6 major cites, not including genoa, give a few hundred thousands worth of gifts to the barmaids then drink with them. Make sure u get her presents. Do this for all the six cities and u should then have completed the memorial album. Claim the prize as well as the title. Relic hunter: exploration rate over 500. Trendsetter (not sure, needs a bit of luck I guess?) cultural C: 30k culture contri. Gladiator: (complete memorial album "right to call yourselves a swordsman? Not sure). Crainio E: 10k noto, filibuster job (might have other requirement not too sure) title can only be changed at pirate ports. Professor of V: 100 reported thesis. Steam explorer: every player who existed in UWO b4 second age will get this title. however, any char created after the update will not get the title. (Getting that title would have something to do with steam I guess) V...of history: participate in historical event. You're welcome

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
The precise conditions for Trendsetter aren't fully known, but there are some definite factors.

1. You can display an ornament in the main hall (costs money and unpredictable due to other players) or in the small galleries (free, lasts one week). Trends can emerge regardless of which gallery you pick to display in, and I've known several people who got the Trendsetter title just from using small galleries, so unless you've got a lot of money, that'd be your best option.

2. Displaying an EA ornament after EA trends have emerged in your city will have no special effect; to gain the title, there must be NO trends currently in your city. You only get the title if trends emerge in your city, because of the ornament you've placed in the museum.

3. Trends seem more likely to emerge based on what ornaments other players of your nation are displaying. If French players are mostly using North Africa trend ornaments, then it's more likely you'll see North Africa trends emerge, than you would Oceania, or EA.

4. The star value of an ornament/discovery has some influence. 5-star ornaments have appeared to be more likely to trigger a trend emerging than a 1-star. Not always, it must be noted, but most of the time that has been the case.

That said, it's pretty random. I've been trying for a year to get Trendsetter with no success, and a friend I invited to the game got it on their second month of playing. (With a 5-star ornament I gave them, incidentally.) In theory, you could always try putting an ornament in a small gallery, wait 24 hours, take it town, put it up again, and rinse-and-repeat until you get a trend. I've never tried this myself, but it could possibly work.

About the Q Title, this is the quest B! meant: Quipucamayoc There are three chains (adventurer, trader, maritimer) that all lead to the same final title-giving quest. Pick whichever one you like (and are best qualified for), then see it through to the end -- the title should be yours soon after you finish the quest. Also, check the comments under that quest, there's a little extra info there that should help you.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body:
For that title, you need Adventure Lv80 + Adventure fame 360,000 or more + 2000 or more discoveries. Discovery accuracy, as I understand it, means your Search/Recognition/E. Research will be successful more often, possibly even on the very first try, despite how difficult the discovery quest might be.

Source: gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?Appellation

comments.body: There is also similar title for battle lvl 80, fame 360k - but i don't have it yet. I've read that it reduces damage from critical shots.

comments.author: BIakeC
comments.body: Theres also one for traders as well. In addition to having reached lvl 80 and having 360k of fame, you also need to have at least 800 mill in your back account, and have at least 40k of contribution points in all four EA nations. The effect from the title is "The Fukkake upper limit of 30%", whatever that's supposed to mean.

comments.author: ThatOneGuy
comments.body:
New title!

Master of Ancient Technologies
A title reserved for those who have greatly contributed to the nation's Ancient Technology Research. Can use the Solar Barge as many times as one likes.

If equipped, the Solar Barge to Atlantis button will show up the next time you enter the docks of your home nation. It showed up for me after two 600 page AT research reports, but it might be unlocked sooner than that. I'd guess it only works until Monday? The title may have to be unlocked again each week, or may not... we'll see!

comments.author: CaliCaddy
comments.body: I just checked and I also had the title. I only submitted one "incomplete" research once at something like 130/100/40 pages. I guess if you submit it once you get the title.

comments.author: Egw
comments.body:
This Master of Ancient Technologies title appears to be tied to your nation's research progress (can be checked with the palace secretary or if you have ancient research ongoing it's shown there on the quest page). So it's more of a national perk rather than an individual perk, or perhaps a combination.

I reported two incomplete researches and a 600/600 one so far. I think I got the title when my nation reached like 22k/50k points or thereabouts and I think I hadn't reported the 600/600 research yet. I suppose you need to have done some research of your own, but the dominating factor seems to be your nation's performance.

Also, if you are online when your nation reaches enough points for you to get the title, you'll get a red text message about it.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body: Just a reminder: Monday (10am OGP time I believe) is when Atlantis moves. Word has it that not only will your nation's ancient tech/solar barge gauge be reduced, but you'll also lose the MOAT title for a bit, likely until you can rebuild the barge, visit Atlantis, and perform research again.

comments.author: BIakeC
comments.body:
To get the Stargazer title, you need to discover all 12 of the Zodiac constellations like Taurus, Libra, etc. The quests are not listed here, but a couple of Japanese guides has them:

gvdb.mydns.jp/db/module/QuestDB/action/DiscoverySearch?fid=18

gvo.gamedb.info/wiki/?Discovery/Astronomy

A fair amount of them have pre-quests as you need to do, and have certain Chrono titles to discover constellations and stars out in the open as well. I know one of them needs the 14th century title which you can only get through discovering Xanadu, which involves an extremely long series of quests to unlock.

comments.author: Morro
comments.body: Actually, there are a few quests that give out the 14th century chrono title outside of the Xanadu chain. "A State of Prayer and Meditation" out of Tunis is a 2 star quest that gives 14th century title. It has a few prereqs: Discovering the city of Salonika, dicovering the city of Ragusa, and completing "Roof and Spine", a 2 star geography quest from Istanbul. MUCH easier than that pesky 64 quest Xanadu chain :D

comments.author: Morro
comments.body: There's also "Investigate the Palace of Menelaus", 3 star Theo quest from Alexandria. Its prereqs are "Story of the Trojan War", 2 star Appraisal quest from Seville and the geography discovery "Pelopponese" from a geography map in from the Lima Scholar.

comments.author: BIakeC
comments.body: Ahh ok, I didnt know that. I guess new quests were added since then that gave the 14th century title without needing to unlock Xanadu.

comments.author: Guilder
comments.body: With a bit of testing, I can confirm that the Deepseeker title is unlocked when you not only reach the 10th floor of an Endless Dungeon (Labyrinth on Crete, Temple of Poseidon in Atlantis), but when you have cleared that floor as well. In other words, the enemies must be gone (fight them or trap-torch them), and the exit to the next floor opens. The title becomes selectable at that point, and no sooner.
